summary: Working in philosophy and religious studies, G. V. Aston completed a PhD in philosophy at the University of Canterbury between 1986 and 2004, studying under Paul Harrison.

G. V. Srinivasa Rao worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Senior Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India until 1945, later retiring as Senior Epigraphical Assistant for the Government Epigraphist for India.

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gadjin Nagao was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hatani and Susumu Yamaguchi, he held the Chair of Buddhist Studies at Kyoto University (1935–1971) and taught at Kyushu University and abroad.

Gail Hinich Sutherland works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and also studied under traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

Gananath Obeyesekere worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Ceylon and University of Washington, he held teaching posts at both institutions before teaching at UC San Diego (~1972–1980) and Princeton University (1980–2000).

Ganesh Prasad was an Indologist and historian who studied at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta. He served as head of department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1905) and held professorships at Banaras Hindu University (~1917–1923) and the University of Calcutta (~1914–1935).

Ganganatha Jha was an Indologist and philosopher. After studies at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Allahabad, he served as professor at Muir Central College (1902–1918), principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1918–1923), and vice chancellor of the University of Allahabad (1923–1932).

Gangzhun is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Qinghai Nationalities University until 1989, he earned a master's degree at Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under MA supervisor Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MPhil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under MA supervisor Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008), and also studied under traditional teacher Lama Byambaa.
Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Garab Dorje Rinpoche studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Garcin de Tassy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Collège de France under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Jean Daniel Kieffer. He held the chair in Indian languages at École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1828–1878).

Gareth Fisher works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. After earning a PhD in socio-cultural anthropology at the University of Virginia in 2006, he served as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

Gareth Sparham is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at McGill, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and the University of British Columbia under Ashok Aklujkar, later teaching Tibetan language at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

Gary A. Tubb is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served on the faculty at Harvard (~1979–1985), taught Sanskrit at Columbia (~1999–2007), and was professor at the University of Chicago from ~2007 until becoming emeritus in ~2021.

Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious and Buddhist studies. Mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Muhammad Daud Rahbar, he served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

Gary Goh Wee Kian works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under supervisor Hui-Chieh Loy, foster supervisor Jay L. Garfield, and teachers Brook Ziporyn, Christopher Anthony Brown, and Cecilia Lim.

Gary Snyder is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley under Chiura Obata and Shih-Hsiang Chen, later serving as professor at UC Davis (1986–2002) and UC Irvine (attested 2002).

Gary Urton is an archaeologist and anthropologist educated at the University of New Mexico and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He taught at Colgate University (1978–2002) and served as Dumbarton Oaks Professor of Pre-Columbian Studies at Harvard University (~2002–2020).

Gaspare Gorresio studied at the University of Turin and under Eugène Burnouf and Stanislas Julien. He taught at the Military Academy of Turin, held Turin's chair in Sanskrit from 1852, and served as director of the National University Library of Turin.
